the final reply and the elapsed time.
# dsh-win-toast-notify
Native Windows toast notification every time a DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) turn finishes — so you can l
ook away from the window while the agent works.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Line 1 is the end reason plus the session title, line 2 is a preview of the turn's final reply, line
3 is where it came from and how long the turn took.
## Requirements
- Windows 10 or 11 (uses the built-in WinRT notification API through Windows PowerShell — no native

module, no build step, no install script).
- A Harness build that emits the `session/event` feed wit

h `turn/end` (dsh 0.2.x).
- Notifications enabled for the app the toast is posted under; Focus assis
t / Do not disturb suppresses it like any other notification.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
or install it from the dsh-market plugin browser. Restart Harness if your build does not reload plug
from the dsh-market plugin browser. Restart Harness if your build does not reload plugin rows live.
## What triggers a toast
The Host half listens to each Session's durable event feed and reacts to `turn/end`:
| `turn/end` reason | Notified by default |

| `completed` | yes — "任务完成" |
| `error` | yes — "任务出错" |
| `blocked` | yes — "任务受阻" |
| `max-tokens

` | yes — "输出达到上限" |
| `interrupted` | yes — "任务被中断" |
| `aborted` (you pressed Stop) | no |
| `fork

"输出达到上限" |
| `interrupted` | yes — "任务被中断" |
| `aborted` (you pressed Stop) | no |
| `forked` | no |
Subagent sessions are skipped by default so a fan-out does not ring once per child.
## Configuration
Edit the row's `config` in the profile patch (or the plugin's settings card), then restart:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## How it works
- **Read-only observer.** The plugin subscribes to `session/event` and keeps only the turn's start t
ime and its last assistant text in memory. It appends no events and writes no files, so fork, resume

and replay are untouched.
- **Host-side only.** No Client module, no DOM, no iframe: the toast is r

aised by the Host, so it also fires when the Web GUI is in a background tab or closed.
- **Toast del
ivery.** `notify()` builds a ToastGeneric XML payload and runs `powershell.exe -EncodedCommand` (UTF
-16LE + Base64) against the WinRT `Windows.UI.Notifications` API, so arbitrary text — Chinese, quote

s, newlines — cannot break the command line.
- **App identity.** Toasts are posted under `com.deepse
ek.dsh` when the desktop app's Start-menu shortcut is present, which makes them appear as DeepSeek H
arness. On a plain `dsh web` or CLI install that AUMID is unregistered and Windows drops the toast s

ilently, so the plugin falls back to the Windows PowerShell AUMID instead.
- **No detaching.** The n
otifier process stays a child of the Host; it exits in about a second. A detached child can be reape
d together with the job object that owns the Host, which loses the notification.
## Limitations

- Windows only. On other platforms the plugin loads and does nothing.
- The toast is attributed to w
hichever app the AUMID belongs to; with the fallback it shows as Windows PowerShell in Action Center

.
- Preview text is plain text: Markdown fences, links, emphasis and inline code are stripped.
